# myinvois-sdk

MyInvois Middleware Gateway

- API version: 0.1.0

- Generator version: 7.10.0

Open-source middleware gateway for Malaysia's MyInvois e-invoicing system.
Provides a simplified REST API layer between applications and the official LHDN MyInvois API.

**Note**: This is an unofficial community project. See DISCLAIMER.md.


  For more information, please visit [https://github.com/user/myinvois-middleware/issues](https://github.com/user/myinvois-middleware/issues)

*Automatically generated by the [OpenAPI Generator](https://openapi-generator.tech)*

## Requirements

Building the API client library requires:

1. Java 11+
2. Maven/Gradle

## Installation

To install the API client library to your local Maven repository, simply execute:

```shell
mvn clean install
```

To deploy it to a remote Maven repository instead, configure the settings of the repository and execute:

```shell
mvn clean deploy
```

Refer to the [OSSRH Guide](http://central.sonatype.org/pages/ossrh-guide.html) for more information.

### Maven users

Add this dependency to your project's POM:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.myinvois</groupId>
  <artifactId>myinvois-sdk</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
  <scope>compile</scope>
</dependency>
```

### Gradle users

Add this dependency to your project's build file:

```groovy
compile "com.myinvois:myinvois-sdk:0.1.0"
```

### Others

At first generate the JAR by executing:

```shell
mvn clean package
```

Then manually install the following JARs:

- `target/myinvois-sdk-0.1.0.jar`
- `target/lib/*.jar`

## Getting Started

```java

import com.myinvois.sdk.*;

import com.myinvois.sdk.api.DocumentsApi;

public class DocumentsApiExample {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        ApiClient defaultClient = Configuration.getDefaultApiClient();
        // Configure clients using the `defaultClient` object, such as
        // overriding the host and port, timeout, etc.
        DocumentsApi apiInstance = new DocumentsApi(defaultClient);
        UUID uuid = UUID.randomUUID(); // UUID | MyInvois document UUID
        DocumentStateChangeRequest documentStateChangeRequest = new DocumentStateChangeRequest(); // DocumentStateChangeRequest | 
        try {
            DocumentStateChangeResponse result = apiInstance.cancelDocument(uuid, documentStateChangeRequest);
            System.out.println(result);
        } catch (ApiException e) {
            System.err.println("Exception when calling DocumentsApi#cancelDocument");
            System.err.println("Status code: " + e.getCode());
            System.err.println("Reason: " + e.getResponseBody());
            System.err.println("Response headers: " + e.getResponseHeaders());
            e.printStackTrace();
        }
    }
}
```

## Recommendation

It's recommended to create an instance of `ApiClient` per thread in a multithreaded environment to avoid any potential issues.
However, the instances of the api clients created from the `ApiClient` are thread-safe and can be re-used.
